title: Git for Global Law
scheme: country (its English name; the ISO 3166-1 code is `code`) / level (federal, national, or an ISO 3166-2 subdivision) / corpus
date_rule: Each corpus is read from its own history at the commit the tree pins: the In-force trailer of each commit is authoritative (git cannot store dates before 1970). Root commits up to 2 November 2026 are in in-force order; since then each one moves pins forward.
future_rule: Most corpora keep laws not yet in force on a future branch; a few keep them on main, dated ahead, and the tools show them only from that date.

corpora.name: Åland law: Landskapslag (2015:68) om hemvårdsstöd
corpora.label: Åland
corpora.record_note: 2015:68 from its original text (in force 2016-01-01) with the 7 amending acts replayed to the Ålex consolidation (updated to ÅFS 2026/31); data retrieved 2026-10-28.
corpora.verification: Verified against official text: the original act ÅFS 2015:68 (first commit) and the current Ålex consolidation (end state, 30/30 sections). The 6 intermediate states between are replays of the ÅFS amending acts and are not independently verified.

scope.when_absent: the amending act prints no transitional or retroactive rule in its commencement provision; the absence is not a statement that the change reaches every case

default_reach.rule: no genuine retroactivity (Constitution of Finland 8 §: nullum crimen; legislative practice otherwise), which binds Åland legislation as well
default_reach.meaning: an act applies from the day it takes effect unless its own commencement provision says otherwise (for instance ÅFS 2023/29, which lets the sibling allowance be granted from 1 August 2022); those provisions are copied verbatim into Applies: trailers
default_reach.authority: Suomen perustuslaki 731/1999, 8 §; Självstyrelselag (1991:71) för Åland; each amending act's commencement provision

default_reach.rule: no retroactivity of restrictive provisions
default_reach.meaning: the Constitution guarantees the principle of the non-retroactivity of provisions that restrict individual rights or that impose a penalty; otherwise a law applies from its entry into force unless it says so

scope.when_absent: this corpus records no scope notes; the absence is not a statement that a change reaches every case

default_reach.rule: a legislative instrument takes effect as its commencement provision says, and an amendment does not disturb what was done before it commenced
default_reach.meaning: the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 and the Legislation Act 2003 apply to Commonwealth instruments; the repeal or amendment of an instrument does not affect its previous operation or any right or liability already acquired or incurred under it, unless a contrary intention appears
default_reach.authority: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 (Cth) s 7(2); Legislation Act 2003 (Cth) Part 2 of Chapter 3; not checked in this corpus

corpora.verification: Verified against official text: every compilation on its compilation day (166 compilations, 0 with mismatches). The comparison is word for word against the register's own Word documents, using a second extractor written separately from the one the build uses. The register's endnotes, the table of contents and running headers are outside the compared text. Because both extractors drop the same apparatus, a second check reads the provision numbers out of each compilation's own table of contents -- the one part the build never reads -- and reports any whose text is nowhere in the tree (166 compilations, 0 with such an entry).
corpora.record_note: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Regulation 2015 (F2015L01854); Competition and Consumer (Notification of Acquisitions) Determination 2025 (F2025L00753); Competition and Consumer (Notification of Acquisitions—Forms) Determination 2025 (F2025L01604); ASIC Corporations (Takeover Bids) Instrument 2023/683 (F2023L01310); Corporations Regulations 2001 (F2001B00274). Compiled text from the Federal Register of Legislation, one commit per compilation on the day it took effect, authored by the amending instrument the register's version record names. Documents retrieved 2026-10-30 to 2026-10-30. Only compilation days are in the record: a change the register dates between two compilations appears on the later compilation's commit. Compilations the register publishes only as legacy .doc or .rtf are not in the record and are not an early block the record starts after; each instrument's no_gaps_from is the day its record becomes continuous, and a date before it may resolve to an earlier committed day.

scope.when_absent: this corpus records no scope notes (no commit carries Applies:); the absence is not a statement that the change reaches every case

default_reach.rule: presumption against retrospectivity; immediate application to procedure
default_reach.meaning: an enactment is presumed not to apply to facts completed before it came into force, or to interfere with vested rights, unless Parliament says so expressly or by necessary implication; procedural provisions apply immediately to pending matters; a repeal does not affect rights acquired or proceedings begun under the repealed enactment; in criminal law, no one may be found guilty of an act that was not an offence when committed, and a person found guilty is entitled to the lesser punishment where it was varied between the offence and sentencing
default_reach.authority: Interpretation Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. I-21, s. 43 (effect of repeal) and s. 44 (repeal and substitution); Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s. 11(g) and 11(i); R. v. Dineley, 2012 SCC 58, [2012] 3 S.C.R. 272; Tran v. Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness), 2017 SCC 50, [2017] 2 S.C.R. 289

default_reach.rule: no retroactivity unless the law says so (法律不遡及の原則)
default_reach.meaning: an amendment applies from its enforcement day (施行日); how it treats facts and proceedings from before that day is set by the transitional provisions (経過措置) in the amending law's supplementary provisions (附則), which this record includes as suppl/<law>.md files but does not read as scope data; the Constitution bars retroactive criminal liability, and the general rule outside criminal law is a principle of interpretation, not a constitutional rule
default_reach.authority: 日本国憲法 第三十九条 ("第三十九条　何人も、実行の時に適法であつた行為又は既に無罪とされた行為については、刑事上の責任を問はれない。又、同一の犯罪について、重ねて刑事上の責任を問はれない。")

citation.note: files are <title folder>/<division>/[<part>/]<chapter>/<section>.md; section numbers are unique within a title (1 CMC § 101 is title-01/general-provisions/chapter-01/101.md).

scope.when_absent: not extracted; effective dates and savings clauses are in the public laws and, where the Commission kept them, in the Commission Comment under each section

default_reach.rule: presumption against retroactivity
default_reach.meaning: a statute operates prospectively unless the legislature clearly says otherwise
default_reach.authority: general rule of statutory construction applied by the CNMI courts

corpora.record_note: The Law Revision Commission publishes only the current text of each section of the Commonwealth Code, one PDF per section, and keeps no dated earlier versions, so each section has one version here (except 23 sections whose earlier PDF is still online at its old address: those have that earlier text first and the current text after it), dated by when the Commission made its PDF (the upload time for sections it amended or added, otherwise the PDF's modification date). That is a compilation date, not the day a law took effect. The Source notes naming each public law are kept as text and listed in data/amendments.csv. A labelled metadata-only correction set records 48 source-supported commencement dates within a conservative subset of simple, unqualified commencement statements. Complex commentary and additional or qualified amendment scope remain held; 3 CMC 4532 executive-order suspensions and 6 CMC 3501 contradictory act-year provenance remain unresolved; 10 CMC § 2933 is not dated to PL 14-41 because its current wording explicitly reflects PL 15-2, § 4. Law text is unchanged. Other sections retain compilation-based dates pending source-supported commencement evidence.
